This contradictory behavior suggests mean compactness may be a spurious correlate or not being properly weighted.

Mean concavity is typically elevated in malignancy. Instance A (541) has 0.1009 (moderate), Instance B (73) has 0.07789 (low), and Instance C (128) has 0.1138 (moderate). This inconsistency suggests concavity is not a reliable pattern for classification in these instances.

Mean symmetry is generally low in malignancy. In Instance C (128), symmetry is 0.2001 (high), and it is misclassified as malignant when true label is benign. Instance B (73) has symmetry 0.1662 (moderate) and is misclassified as benign. This shows that increased symmetry, which typically suggests benignity, leads to incorrect malignant predictions, possibly indicating model inversion in symmetry usage.
